definition: A geneware or BCI licensing clause in which agreeing to one procedure automatically enrolls the patient in a tiered series of follow-up treatments, data-sharing agreements, and proprietary dependency protocols. Widely considered predatory; widely practiced.
origin: Helix Biosystems and Sterling-Nakamura legal contract language
usage: Medical ethicists, legal advocates, patients discovering the clause after the fact
example: She signed for a standard nerve sleeve and didn't realize cascade consent had her locked into six years of Sterling-Nakamura proprietary calibrations.
